classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires recognising two isosceles triangles from equal half-diagonals and linking their angle sums through a straight angle, without assuming right angles at the corners.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in these diagrams.

spec.description: Triangle with a vertical right side and three exterior-angle extensions; ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angles 114 degrees and 134 degrees; unknown exterior angle alpha at the upper-right vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
The left and lower-right interior angles are $180^\circ-114^\circ=66^\circ$ and $180^\circ-134^\circ=46^\circ$ (straight angles).

The exterior angle equals the sum of the opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=66^\circ+46^\circ\\\alpha&=112^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Overlapping triangles with a horizontal base; 24-degree label retains its curved leader to the narrow upper angle.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left crossing angle 102 degrees, lower-right angle 44 degrees, upper angle 24 degrees; alpha at the further-right vertex and beta above the horizontal base.

answer.worked:
The crossing angle inside the upper-right triangle is $180^\circ-102^\circ=78^\circ$ (straight angle).

Using the angle sum of that triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+24^\circ+78^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=78^\circ\end{align*}$$
The crossing angle inside the lower triangle is $78^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\beta+78^\circ+44^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=58^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle with one matching tick on each sloping side.
spec.mathematics: Apex angle alpha; right base angle 4 alpha; equal base angles follow from the marked equal sides.

answer.worked:
Both base angles are $4\alpha$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+4\alpha+4\alpha&=180^\circ\\9\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rectangular-looking unmarked outline with two red dashed diagonals and four identical half-diagonal ticks. No right-angle or parallel marks are added.
spec.mathematics: All four half-diagonals are equal. Top-right angle between top edge and diagonal is 38 degrees; alpha is the left central angle, beta the upper central angle, gamma the top-left angle beside the left edge.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original marks, givens and unknown labels.

answer.short:
$\alpha=76^\circ$, $\beta=104^\circ$, $\gamma=52^\circ$

Use the equal half-diagonals to identify isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
The upper triangle has equal sides from the diagonal intersection to the top corners, so both base angles are $38^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta+38^\circ+38^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=104^\circ\end{align*}$$
At the intersection, adjacent angles form a straight angle.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+104^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
The left triangle also has equal sides from the intersection to its two corners, so its base angles are both $\gamma$.
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+\gamma+76^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\gamma&=104^\circ\\\gamma&=52^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Irregular quadrilateral with all four interior angles expressed as multiples of alpha.
spec.mathematics: Angles in source order from bottom left: alpha, 4 alpha, 3 alpha, 2 alpha.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+4\alpha+3\alpha+2\alpha&=360^\circ\\10\alpha&=360^\circ\\\alpha&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram with single arrows on the vertical sides and double arrows on the sloping sides; reflex angle outside the lower-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: Reflex angle 230 degrees and interior alpha at lower left; beta at upper left and gamma at upper right.

answer.worked:
Angles in a revolution add to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+230^\circ&=360^\circ\\\alpha&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles between the parallel sloping sides add to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta+130^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles between the parallel vertical sides add to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+50^\circ&=180^\circ\\\gamma&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$
